literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该研究描述了 NiVG 和 NiVF 的结构,并检查了它们与人类受体和单克隆抗体 Fab 66 的相互作用。它还探索了在不同国家发现的类似糖蛋白。 [10.64898/2026.09.02.748953]
其中苦艾酒、环表太冷素和薯蓣皂苷元显示出最有利的相互作用结果。 [10.1038/s41598-026-66632-9]
审查得出的结论是,尼帕病毒 是一种极其危险的人畜共患病毒,具有复发性 暴发 的特点,其特点是病死率高、严重的神经和呼吸系统疾病以及缺乏有效的 治疗 选择。它强调了了解导致病毒 跨物种溢出 和人传人 传播 的生态和人为因素的重要性。 [10.18231/j.ijmmtd.15094.1788324291]
两份血清样本的 尼帕病毒 抗体呈阳性,表明 患病率 为 1.45%(95% CI:0.4–5.13%)。测试样本中未检测到加纳病毒抗体。 [10.3390/v18090961]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study described the structures of NiVG and NiVF and examined their interactions with human receptors and monoclonal antibody Fab 66. It also explored similar glycoproteins found in different countries. [10.64898/2026.09.02.748953]
Among which Absinthin, Cycloepiatalantin, and Diosgenin showed the most favorable interactions results. [10.1038/s41598-026-66632-9]

news.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 东京大学宣布即将启动 疫苗 针对 尼帕病毒 的临床试验。这种疾病具有高度致命性,可对神经和呼吸系统造成严重损害。目前全球范围内尚无经批准的有效针对该病毒的 疫苗。 [news-c14e803f123e56cc]
卫生专家强调,东盟需要建立一个联合系统来应对流行病、人畜共患疾病和抗菌素耐药性(AMR)等健康威胁。尼帕病毒 被认为是能够在各国迅速传播的病原体之一。 [news-fe128e28ef6b3de2]
印度尼西亚进行了一场大流行模拟演习,以测试其对新“疾病 X”的准备情况,虚构了致命的“尼帕-X”病毒在几天内从受感染的牲畜传播给人类的案例,其中包括作为 传播 活动的国际音乐节。此次演习由印尼卫生部和CEPI共同主办。 [news-8485d1aecafc3f8d]
该报告讨论了尼日利亚用蝙蝠作为传统药物的贸易,强调了人畜共患疾病 传播 的风险。它引用了 2023 年的一项研究,该研究在稻草色 果蝠 中发现了抗体,表明接触过 亨尼帕病毒 谱系 GH-M74a、尼帕病毒 和蝙蝠流感 H17N10。该报告还提到了 2025 年的一项研究,显示蝙蝠贸易参与者的卫生习惯不佳。 [news-7f798678bd85d77c]
政府向因印度尼西亚森林火灾而受到雾霾影响的菲律宾人发布了健康警告和保护措施。卫生部 (DOH) 警告说,接触雾霾可能会导致呼吸困难、咳嗽、胸痛、眼睛刺激或流泪。它还可能使现有的肺部疾病(例如哮喘)恶化。卫生部为大部分时间在路上的通勤者和工人(包括送货骑手和现场工作人员)分享了保护自己免受雾霾天气影响的建议。 [news-42e1fa0c86245a8a]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Nipah virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The University of Tokyo announced the upcoming launch of clinical trials for a vaccine against the Nipah virus. The disease is highly fatal and can cause severe damage to the nervous and respiratory systems. There is currently no approved effective vaccine against this virus worldwide. [news-c14e803f123e56cc]

Health experts emphasized the need for Asean to develop a joint system to address health threats such as pandemics, zoonotic diseases, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The Nipah virus was cited as one of the pathogens capable of spreading rapidly across countries. [news-fe128e28ef6b3de2]

Indonesia conducted a pandemic simulation exercise to test its readiness for a new 'Disease X', with a fictional case of a deadly 'Nipah-X' virus spreading from infected livestock to people within days, including an international music festival as a transmission event. [news-8485d1aecafc3f8d]

The report discusses the trade of bats for traditional medicine in Nigeria, highlighting the risk of zoonotic disease transmission. It references a 2023 study that found antibodies in straw-coloured fruit bats indicating exposure to henipavirus lineage GH-M74a, Nipah virus, and bat influenza H17N10. [news-7f798678bd85d77c]

The government issued health warnings and protective measures for Filipinos affected by haze due to forest fires in Indonesia. The Department of Health (DOH) warned that exposure to haze may cause difficulty breathing, coughing, chest pain, eye irritation or watery eyes. [news-42e1fa0c86245a8a]

papers.title: Structural Aspects of Nipah Virus Glycoproteins using Predictive Protein Modeling
papers.abstract: Nipah is a virus borne zoonotic disease that mostly occurs in Southeast Asian countries. Nipah virus (NiV) infection is potentially lethal as it can cause fatal encephalitis, and as of now, there are no vaccines or therapeutic treatments for this disease. The highly pathogenic NiV belongs to the Paramyxovirus family and the natural host of NiV is fruit bats of the Pteropodidae family. Though NiV has not been detected in the US, rather recently the Camp Hill virus (CHV) in shrew species was identified in Camp Hill, Alabama. This virus is characteristically similar to Nipah, and belongs to the henipavirus genus that include the Nipah and Hendra viruses. NiV has two surface glycoproteins namely the attachment glycoprotein (NiVG) and the fusion glycoprotein (NiVF). Being associated with host cell attachment and fusion of viral membrane, these glycoproteins tend to facilitate the viral entry to the host cell. The present paper describes the structures of the aforesaid viral glycoproteins based on the available database of protein structures and examines if they have an evolutionary link to other viral glycoproteins. Certain similar glycoproteins found in different countries are also explored. The structure-function relationship for these two NiV glycoproteins are determined using time-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The interfacial ligand-receptor interactions between NiV proteins with human receptor and monoclonal antibody, Fab 66, are examined. A primary motivation for these structural studies is that the results might potentially contribute to future therapeutic developments and drug designs to effectively combat NiV.

papers.title: Computational identification of multi-targeted bioactive phytocompounds as candidate drug molecules against Nipah virus infection
papers.abstract: Nipah Virus (NiV) is a highly virulent zoonotic virus that leads to severe encephalitis and respiratory diseases with mortality rates estimated at 40–75%, sometimes up to 100% in specific outbreaks. NiV has outbreaks in South and Southeast Asia, particularly in Bangladesh, India, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, and so on. The WHO classifies NiV as a priority pathogen due to its high fatality rate, lack of approved antiviral drugs or vaccines, and pandemic potential spread by human-to-human transmission. Therefore, identifying novel therapeutic agents against NiV remains a critical global health priority now. Natural phytochemicals have gained increasing attention due to their diverse biological activities and, favorable safety profiles. In this study, we investigated 2271 unique phytocompounds as drug candidates induced from 261 medicinal plants having high antiviral activities through molecular docking interaction with the NiV G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and L protein. Phytocompounds with significant binding affinity (< − 7.0 kcal/mol) were further assessed by, drug-likeness screening, ADME/T Profiling, network pharmacology, protein–ligand interaction analysis, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and 100 ns MD simulation to investigate structural stability and interaction behavior. Docking results revealed strong binding affinity of several phytochemicals toward NiV proteins. Among which Absinthin, Cycloepiatalantin, and Diosgenin showed the most favorable interactions results. ADME/T analysis suggested high absorption, low predicted toxicity, and effective blood–brain barrier penetration. DFT analysis indicated a favorable electronic interaction potential of the phytochemicals. MD simulations suggested stable protein–ligand complexes supported by the following analysis, RMSD, RMSF, SASA, RoG, MM-PBSA, DCCM, and PCA. Overall, these findings suggest that these Phytocompounds may serve as potential candidates for further experimental validation as antiviral agents against NiV. Using large-scale Phytocompounds screening, this study identified candidate compounds with predicted bioactivity capable of interacting with NiV proteins, while helping to reduce the cost, time, and labor associated with conventional wet-laboratory experiments.

source_records.abstract: Nipah Virus (NiV) is a highly virulent zoonotic virus that leads to severe encephalitis and respiratory diseases with mortality rates estimated at 40–75%, sometimes up to 100% in specific outbreaks. NiV has outbreaks in South and Southeast Asia, particularly in Bangladesh, India, Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, and so on. The WHO classifies NiV as a priority pathogen due to its high fatality rate, lack of approved antiviral drugs or vaccines, and pandemic potential spread by human-to-human transmission. Therefore, identifying novel therapeutic agents against NiV remains a critical global health priority now. Natural phytochemicals have gained increasing attention due to their diverse biological activities and, favorable safety profiles. In this study, we investigated 2271 unique phytocompounds as drug candidates induced from 261 medicinal plants having high antiviral activities through molecular docking interaction with the NiV G glycoprotein, F fusion protein, and L protein. Phytocompounds with significant binding affinity (< − 7.0 kcal/mol) were further assessed by, drug-likeness screening, ADME/T Profiling, network pharmacology, protein–ligand interaction analysis, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and 100 ns MD simulation to investigate structural stability and interaction behavior. Docking results revealed strong binding affinity of several phytochemicals toward NiV proteins. Among which Absinthin, Cycloepiatalantin, and Diosgenin showed the most favorable interactions results. ADME/T analysis suggested high absorption, low predicted toxicity, and effective blood–brain barrier penetration. DFT analysis indicated a favorable electronic interaction potential of the phytochemicals. MD simulations suggested stable protein–ligand complexes supported by the following analysis, RMSD, RMSF, SASA, RoG, MM-PBSA, DCCM, and PCA. Overall, these findings suggest that these Phytocompounds may serve as potential candidates for further experimental validation as antiviral agents against NiV. Using large-scale Phytocompounds screening, this study identified candidate compounds with predicted bioactivity capable of interacting with NiV proteins, while helping to reduce the cost, time, and labor associated with conventional wet-laboratory experiments.

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是一种高毒力的人畜共患病毒,可导致严重的 脑炎 和呼吸道疾病,死亡率 的发病率估计为 40-75%,有时在特定的 暴发 中高达 100%。NiV 在南亚和东南亚设有 暴发,特别是在孟加拉国、印度、菲律宾、马来西亚、新加坡等。由于死亡率高、缺乏批准的 抗病毒药物 药物或 疫苗 以及 传播 可能在人与人之间传播,世界卫生组织将 NiV 列为优先病原体。因此,寻找针对 NiV 的新型治疗药物仍然是当前全球健康的一个重要优先事项。天然植物化学物质因其多样化的生物活性和良好的安全性而受到越来越多的关注。在这项研究中,我们通过与 NiV G 糖蛋白、F 融合蛋白和 L 蛋白的分子对接相互作用,研究了 261 种具有高 抗病毒药物 活性的药用植物诱导的 2271 种独特的植物化合物作为候选药物。通过药物相似性筛选、ADME/T 分析、网络药理学、蛋白质-配体相互作用分析、密度泛函理论 (DFT) 计算和 100 ns MD 模拟来进一步评估具有显着结合亲和力 (< − 7.0 kcal/mol) 的植物化合物,以研究结构稳定性和相互作用行为。对接结果显示几种植物化学物质对 NiV 蛋白具有很强的结合亲和力。其中苦艾酒、环表太冷素和薯蓣皂苷元显示出最有利的相互作用结果。ADME/T 分析表明吸收率高,预测毒性低,并且能有效穿透血脑屏障。DFT 分析表明植物化学物质具有良好的电子相互作用潜力。MD 模拟表明稳定的蛋白质-配体复合物得到以下分析的支持:RMSD、RMSF、SASA、RoG、MM-PBSA、DCCM 和 PCA。总的来说,这些发现表明这些植物化合物可以作为进一步实验验证的潜在候选物,作为抗 NiV 的 抗病毒药物 药物。通过大规模植物化合物筛选,本研究确定了具有预测生物活性、能够与 NiV 蛋白相互作用的候选化合物,同时有助于减少与传统湿实验室实验相关的成本、时间和劳动力。

papers.title: Nipah virus: Current knowledge and the need for one health approach – A comprehensive review
papers.abstract: An extremely dangerous zoonotic virus, the Nipah virus (NiV) belonging to the genus Henipavirus and family Paramyxoviridae continues to be a major threat to the world health. Recurrent outbreaks of NiV have been marked by high case fatality rates, severe neurological and respiratory illness, and a lack of effective treatment options since the virus first appeared in the late 1990s. The review offers an updated and comprehensive information on virus biology, epidemiology, transmission channels, clinical manifestations, diagnostic techniques, and public health consequences, conceptually taken from previous studies and the mass of information contained within. The growing significance of human-to-human transmission and an understanding of the ecological and anthropogenic factors underlying viral spillover are of special attention. In order to reduce the danger of future outbreaks, the analysis also identifies gaps in surveillance, diagnostics, and countermeasure development, highlighting the necessity of coordinated One Health policies.
papers.journal: IP International Journal of Medical Microbiology and Tropical Diseases

papers.title: Limited Antibodies to Henipaviruses Detected Among Nigerian Horses Using Pseudotyped Virus Neutralization Tests
papers.abstract: The Hendra virus (HeV; Henipavirus hendraense) and Nipah virus (NiV; Henipavirus nipahense), members of the genus Henipavirus, are high-consequence pathogens that have caused multiple zoonotic outbreaks with high mortality. Frequently, pigs or horses have acted as bridging hosts between bats, the reservoir hosts, and people. We used pseudotyped viruses with the fusion (F) and glycoprotein (G) envelope proteins of the NiV and Ghana virus (GhV; Henipavirus ghanaense) in neutralization tests (PVNTs) to screen serum samples from 138 apparently healthy horses in northwest Nigeria. No antibodies to GhV were detected in the 138 samples tested. Two serum samples were positive for antibodies to NiV on an initial screen using a single serum dilution, giving a prevalence of 1.45% (95% CI: 0.4–5.13%). Both positive samples were from female, non-local breeds of horses that were used for polo and were 15 and 20 years old. The only significant risk factor found through Chi-squared analysis was the older age category (p = 0.028). On titration in a PVNT, a half-maximal inhibitory concentration was calculated for both samples (IC50 = 11.6 and 16.8). These data suggest the limited exposure of horses to NiV in the sample region but confirms that horses can act as a sentinel population for the circulation of henipaviruses.

Using pseudotyped virus neutralization tests, serum samples from 138 healthy horses were analyzed. Two samples were positive for Nipah virus antibodies, indicating a low prevalence of 1.45% (95% CI: 0.4–5.13%). No antibodies to Ghana virus were found. These findings contribute to understanding Nipah virus epidemiology and support the use of horses in monitoring henipavirus activity.

papers.abstract_zh: 亨德拉病毒(HeV;亨尼帕病毒 hendraense)和 尼帕病毒(NiV;亨尼帕病毒 nipahense)是 亨尼帕病毒 属的成员,是引起多种人畜共患 死亡率 的高后果病原体。通常,猪或马充当蝙蝠、储存宿主 宿主 和人类之间的桥梁。我们在中和试验 (PVNT) 中使用具有 NiV 和加纳病毒 (GhV;亨尼帕病毒 ghanaense) 融合 (F) 和糖蛋白 (G) 包膜蛋白的假型病毒来筛选来自尼日利亚西北部 138 匹表面健康的马的血清样本。在测试的 138 个样本中未检测到 GhV 抗体。使用单一血清稀释液进行初始筛选时,两份血清样本的 NiV 抗体呈阳性,患病率 为 1.45%(95% CI:0.4–5.13%)。两个阳性样本均来自用于马球比赛的非本地品种的雌性马,年龄分别为 15 岁和 20 岁。通过卡方分析发现的唯一显着风险因素是年龄较大的类别(p = 0.028)。在 PVNT 中滴定时,计算两个样品的半最大抑制浓度(IC50 = 11.6 和 16.8)。这些数据表明,样本区域中马匹对 NiV 的暴露有限,但证实马匹可以充当 亨尼帕病毒 循环的哨兵群体。

news.content_title: Indonesia steps up Southeast Asia’s outbreak preparedness with pandemic simulation exercise
news.content: Securing the future: CEPI's 3.0 Investment Case Find out moreDismiss About What we do Partner with us Our impact News & stories Contact us CEPI Indonesia steps up Southeast Asia’s outbreak preparedness with pandemic simulation exercise CEPI3rd September 2026 Share JAKARTA, 3 SEP 2026—Indonesia is advancing Southeast Asia’s readiness to tackle a future epidemic or pandemic threat by conducting a landmark pandemic simulation exercise that will strengthen efforts to rapidly develop safe and effective vaccines and other tools against a new ‘Disease X’. Over 120 experts working across the vaccine and epidemic preparedness research ecosystem in Indonesia and the region took part in the table-top event launching today in Jakarta. The event is co-hosted by the Indonesian Ministry of Health and the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), the global organisation dedicated to transforming the world’s response to epidemic and pandemic threats. The event seeks to build on Indonesia and CEPI’s shared vision to better prepare the world to face emerging infectious disease outbreaks. This vision is built on advancing scientific research, technology and cooperation to create the tools to reduce epidemic and pandemic risks. “If we know that a threat can kill millions or even billions of our brothers and sisters, then we must be prepared for it. We must do the same—or better—to prepare for the next war against disease by investing seriously in saving lives,” said Budi Gunadi Sadikin, Indonesia’s Minister of Health during the Opening Session 100 Days Mission Table Top Exercise in Jakarta, on Thursday September 3rd. Minister Budi continued, “As we host this landmark simulation exercise with CEPI, we are actively stress-testing our national capabilities—from deploying Point-of-Care Testing devices across our primary health centres to strengthening our genome sequencing network. Achieving the 100 Days Mission requires us to build robust scientific, surveillance, manufacturing and regulatory ecosystems. Through strategic partnerships and enhanced preparedness, Indonesia is proud to lead the way in ensuring our region and the world are ready to tackle the next 'Disease X'.” Alongside experts from across academic and private organisations, including specialists in areas such as virus surveillance, laboratory testing, clinical trials, Artificial Intelligence, biosecurity, manufacturing, regulatory, access and policy, event attendees include Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, Indonesian Food and Drug Authority, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and WHO Indonesia. Representatives from health ministries and regulatory bodies across Malaysia, Singapore, and Australia were also in attendance as observers to the event to leverage lessons learned from the exercise for their own national outbreak preparedness. The exercise will present a fictional case of a deadly never-before-seen ‘Nipah-X’ outbreak, a pathogen related to the deadly bat-borne Nipah virus which is known to affect the region. The scenario imagines a fictitious ‘Nipah-X’ virus spreading from infected livestock to people within days, with cases rapidly escalating through events including an international music festival. Experts will be invited to explore, discuss and share feedback on how they can collaborate and leverage the full breadth of Indonesia’s pandemic preparedness capability and infrastructure to rapidly develop a new vaccine in as little as 100 days from identifying the new disease. The 100-day vaccine target, known as the 100 Days Mission, is a goal spearheaded by CEPI and embraced by the G7 and G20 nations – including Indonesia – that aims to compress the time it takes to develop a vaccine against a newly-identified virus to a third of the time it took to create the first COVID-19 vaccines. Acting within 100 days could help stop a pandemic in its tracks and enable vaccine doses to reach those who need them most in a public health emergency. “Indonesia has established itself as a globally recognised force within vaccine manufacturing and health security, so this pandemic simulation exercise serves as a prime opportunity to work with leading experts across Indonesia’s vaccine chain to plan local responses to an imagined viral threat,” explains Dr Richard Hatchett, CEO of CEPI. “The world could have saved more than 8 million lives and avoided trillions in economic losses if a COVID-19 vaccine had been developed within 100 days. That is exactly why exercises like this are so important: they stress-test our vaccine response and containment strategies, helping ensure we can respond faster and more effectively when the next health emergency strikes.” The exercise, running over two days this week, is one of a series CEPI is hosting with Governments and partners around the world to map and test out readiness to conduct a rapid vaccine R&D response to a novel virus outbreak as part of its new strategy, launching next year, which aims to transform the world’s response to epidemic and pandemic threats. Learnings from this exercise will help strengthen Indonesia’s ability to respond to future outbreaks and reflects a core ambition of CEPI’s new strategy to make the 100 Days Mission a reality by testing and building national and regional response capabilities before the next pandemic. Indonesia is a key partner to and investor in CEPI. The Government of Indonesia has provided US$6 million in funding to advance CEPI’s investments in innovative research and technologies against known disease threats and a future ‘Disease X’. Indonesia’s national vaccine manufacturer, Bio Farma, which services over 130 countries worldwide, is also a member of CEPI’s vaccine manufacturing facility network which seeks to increase emerging disease vaccine capacity and capabilities in the Global South. Achieving the 100 Days Mission requires us to build robust scientific, surveillance, manufacturing and regulatory ecosystems. Through strategic partnerships and enhanced preparedness, Indonesia is proud to lead the way in ensuring our region and the world are ready to tackle the next 'Disease X'.” Alongside experts from across academic and private organisations, including specialists in areas such as virus surveillance, laboratory testing, clinical trials, Artificial Intelligence, biosecurity, manufacturing, regulatory, access and policy, event attendees include Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, Indonesian Food and Drug Authority, Ministry of Agriculture, Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and WHO Indonesia. Representatives from health ministries and regulatory bodies across Malaysia, Singapore, and Australia were also in attendance as observers to the event to leverage lessons learned from the exercise for their own national outbreak preparedness. The exercise will present a fictional case of a deadly never-before-seen ‘Nipah-X’ outbreak, a pathogen related to the deadly bat-borne Nipah virus which is known to affect the region. The scenario imagines a fictitious ‘Nipah-X’ virus spreading from infected livestock to people within days, with cases rapidly escalating through events including an international music festival. Experts will be invited to explore, discuss and share feedback on how they can collaborate and leverage the full breadth of Indonesia’s pandemic preparedness capability and infrastructure to rapidly develop a new vaccine in as little as 100 days from identifying the new disease. The 100-day vaccine target, known as the 100 Days Mission, is a goal spearheaded by CEPI and embraced by the G7 and G20 nations – including Indonesia – that aims to compress the time it takes to develop a vaccine against a newly-identified virus to a third of the time it took to create the first COVID-19 vaccines. Acting within 100 days could help stop a pandemic in its tracks and enable vaccine doses to reach those who need them most in a public health emergency. “Indonesia has established itself as a globally recognised force within vaccine manufacturing and health security, so this pandemic simulation exercise serves as a prime opportunity to work with leading experts across Indonesia’s vaccine chain to plan local responses to an imagined viral threat,” explains Dr Richard Hatchett, CEO of CEPI. “The world could have saved more than 8 million lives and avoided trillions in economic losses if a COVID-19 vaccine had been developed within 100 days. That is exactly why exercises like this are so important: they stress-test our vaccine response and containment strategies, helping ensure we can respond faster and more effectively when the next health emergency strikes.” The exercise, running over two days this week, is one of a series CEPI is hosting with Governments and partners around the world to map and test out readiness to conduct a rapid vaccine R&D response to a novel virus outbreak as part of its new strategy, launching next year, which aims to transform the world’s response to epidemic and pandemic threats. Learnings from this exercise will help strengthen Indonesia’s ability to respond to future outbreaks and reflects a core ambition of CEPI’s new strategy to make the 100 Days Mission a reality by testing and building national and regional response capabilities before the next pandemic. Indonesia is a key partner to and investor in CEPI. The Government of Indonesia has provided US$6 million in funding to advance CEPI’s investments in innovative research and technologies against known disease threats and a future ‘Disease X’. Indonesia’s national vaccine manufacturer, Bio Farma, which services over 130 countries worldwide, is also a member of CEPI’s vaccine manufacturing facility network which seeks to increase emerging disease vaccine capacity and capabilities in the Global South. PETALING JAYA: Asean must strengthen regional coordination to confront pandemics, zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and other health threats that cannot be contained within national borders, health experts say. Prof Dr Zaleha Md Isa of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia said individual national policies are insufficient to address public health risks that exploit porous borders, regulatory differences and shared ecosystems. Among the most pressing threats, she said, are pandemics and zoonotic outbreaks, with pathogens such as avian influenza, Nipah virus and emerging coronaviruses capable of spreading rapidly across countries. “Isolated national border closures or unilateral testing protocols fail without real-time, shared epidemiological surveillance and joint rapid-containment strategies,” she said when contacted. She said Asean needs a coordinated One Health surveillance system linking human, animal and environmental health, alongside stronger regional laboratory networks and harmonised regulations to combat AMR. Differences in rules governing antibiotic sales, veterinary drug use and agricultural practices could undermine an individual country’s efforts as resistant pathogens spread through travel, trade, livestock and shared waterways. Zaleha said Malaysia, as chair of the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting which starts today, should push for more concrete commitments, including stronger pathogen and AMR data-sharing, pooled procurement and medical stockpiles, and the full operationalisation of the Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases. StarPicks When a loved one falls ill, questions follow Public health physician Dr Rozita Hod pointed to the transboundary haze as an immediate regional health threat requiring coordinated action involving multiple agencies and neighbouring countries. She said technical assistance and resources should be extended to countries that need them, adding that solid waste management is another issue requiring attention. Economist Emeritus Prof Dr Barjoyai Bardai said the economic risks go beyond infectious diseases, with ageing populations and shortages of healthcare workers representing Asean’s biggest long-term challenge. An ageing population would increase healthcare and long-term care expenditure while shrinking the productive workforce and shortages of doctors, nurses, caregivers and public health professionals would further strain the health system, he said. Barjoyai described AMR as potentially the region’s “most expensive silent crisis”, warning that drug-resistant infections could drive up healthcare costs and reduce labour productivity. Future pandemics also remained a major systemic economic risk after Covid-19 showed how quickly a health emergency could disrupt trade, tourism, manufacturing, education and public finances. “The biggest health challenge for Asean is not any single disease but the combination of ageing populations, workforce shortages, antimicrobial resistance and future health shocks,” he said. Singapore 29 Aug 2026 Southern Asean haze highlights need for stronger firefighting... PETALING JAYA: Asean must strengthen regional coordination to confront pandemics, zoonotic diseases, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and other health threats that cannot be contained within national borders, health experts say. Prof Dr Zaleha Md Isa of Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia said individual national policies are insufficient to address public health risks that exploit porous borders, regulatory differences and shared ecosystems. Among the most pressing threats, she said, are pandemics and zoonotic outbreaks, with pathogens such as avian influenza, Nipah virus and emerging coronaviruses capable of spreading rapidly across countries. “Isolated national border closures or unilateral testing protocols fail without real-time, shared epidemiological surveillance and joint rapid-containment strategies,” she said when contacted. She said Asean needs a coordinated One Health surveillance system linking human, animal and environmental health, alongside stronger regional laboratory networks and harmonised regulations to combat AMR. Differences in rules governing antibiotic sales, veterinary drug use and agricultural practices could undermine an individual country’s efforts as resistant pathogens spread through travel, trade, livestock and shared waterways. Zaleha said Malaysia, as chair of the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting which starts today, should push for more concrete commitments, including stronger pathogen and AMR data-sharing, pooled procurement and medical stockpiles, and the full operationalisation of the Asean Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases. StarPicks When a loved one falls ill, questions follow Public health physician Dr Rozita Hod pointed to the transboundary haze as an immediate regional health threat requiring coordinated action involving multiple agencies and neighbouring countries. She said technical assistance and resources should be extended to countries that need them, adding that solid waste management is another issue requiring attention. Economist Emeritus Prof Dr Barjoyai Bardai said the economic risks go beyond infectious diseases, with ageing populations and shortages of healthcare workers representing Asean’s biggest long-term challenge. An ageing population would increase healthcare and long-term care expenditure while shrinking the productive workforce and shortages of doctors, nurses, caregivers and public health professionals would further strain the health system, he said. Barjoyai described AMR as potentially the region’s “most expensive silent crisis”, warning that drug-resistant infections could drive up healthcare costs and reduce labour productivity. Future pandemics also remained a major systemic economic risk after Covid-19 showed how quickly a health emergency could disrupt trade, tourism, manufacturing, education and public finances. “The biggest health challenge for Asean is not any single disease but the combination of ageing populations, workforce shortages, antimicrobial resistance and future health shocks,” he said. ILORIN, Nigeria — Near the Emir Palace in Nigeria’s Oja-Oba market, a powerful thunderstorm toppled a large strangler fig tree in early July. The tree had long been home to a colony of straw-coloured fruit bats, many of which were injured in the fall. Two children, aged 9 and 12, saw a business opportunity. The bats soon ended up at the roadside stall of a Yoruba traditional medicine ingredient trader who prefers to be called “Iya Kabirat.” For 50 years, she has sold assorted barks, herbs, animal carcasses, skins, and other materials used by herbalists for spiritual healing. She buys each bat from the children for 500 naira ($0.36), and sells it to customers for 700 naira ($0.50). “I was born in this business,” says Kabirat. “Many herbalists regularly come here to buy them. Traditional healers use their flesh to prepare concoctions for women battling infertility.” This reporter visited three such shops where bats were being sold to treat various ailments. Let’s Dig Deep Together. Subscribe to The Xylom's free newsletters to get more updates on the world's most pressing health and environmental disparities. Across western Nigeria, bats are incorporated into traditional medicine for spiritual healing. The recipes entail charring their flesh and grinding it into a fine powder. The country is home to roughly 100 bat species, making up one-third of the 266 species found in sub-Saharan Africa. But these statistics are lost on locals who depend on bats for their meat. In neighbouring urban hubs such as Lagos, Calabar and Port Harcourt, bats are considered a delicacy and are sold openly by bushmeat vendors. In Ilorin, however, they are sought-after ingredients in traditional medicine. Often reservoirs for severe infectious diseases, bats can transmit pathogens to humans, raising concerns among researchers about the potential for zoonotic disease transmission. A 2023 study examined 304 straw-coloured fruit bats (Eidolon helvum) captured for human consumption in Makurdi, Nigeria. Researchers found antibodies indicating exposure to henipavirus lineage GH-M74a, Nipah virus, and bat influenza H17N10. The researchers said the findings pointed to a potential risk of zoonotic spillover associated with the hunting and consumption of bats. Researchers found antibodies indicating exposure to henipavirus lineage GH-M74a, Nipah virus, and bat influenza H17N10 in straw-coloured fruit bats. (Jan Vršovský/Wikimedia Commons) The Risk of Bat-Hunting Reports estimate that nearly 20% of sub-Saharan bat species are hunted for food and medicine. While bats may provide nutritional benefits, researchers say the health risks can outweigh them. Bat meat contains protein and essential nutrients such as iron and B vitamins, says Uju Onuorah, a registered dietitian-nutritionist and research associate at Nutrition Drive for Healthy Diet Initiative. “[But, they] are also known reservoirs for several viruses and pathogens that can be transmitted to humans, particularly during hunting, slaughtering, and preparation.” From hunting and handling to preparation, every step of the bat meat trade poses a risk of exposure to zoonotic diseases. (Abdullahi Jimoh for The Xylom) Limited knowledge of zoonotic diseases among hunters, traders, and consumers can increase the risk of transmission. A 2025 study found that people across the value chain often lacked personal protective equipment and practiced poor hand hygiene, further increasing their exposure risk. While cooking bat meat thoroughly can reduce the risk of foodborne pathogens, it does not eliminate exposure risks during hunting, handling, and preparation, Onuorah points out. “Public health experts generally discourage the hunting and consumption of bats, especially in areas where zoonotic diseases are a concern,” she adds. Like many others in Oyo, Oyelami Opeyemi, 35, hunted birds and bats as a child. A catapult hobbyist, he would use a stone and the elastic band of his Y-shaped wooden weapon to shoot bats. Opeyemi still eats bats and describes their flavour as “sweet.” “We used to hunt them in the morning or at night,” he says, adding that he and other bat hunters were unaware of the disease risks because none of them had fallen ill or contracted a disease. When the Law of the Land Falls Short Bats are among the world’s most misunderstood nocturnal mammals. They navigate in darkness using echolocation, producing high-pitched sounds that bounce off objects and help them locate their prey. These mammals play a vital role in the country’s biodiversity, providing key ecosystem services such as pollination, seed dispersal and insect control. Their role is indispensable for agriculture. “Nigeria is one of Africa’s most important countries for bat conservation,” says Olajumoke Morenikeji, a parasitology professor at the University of Ibadan. The country’s bat diversity is reflected in the work of ecologist Iroro Tanshi, whose search through cave networks led to the rediscovery of a short-tailed roundleaf bat, a species that had not been spotted in the wild for more than three decades. Earlier this year, Tanshi was awarded the Goldman Prize for her conservation work. Fruit bats face threats ranging from hunting for bushmeat and traditional medicine to habitat loss caused by deforestation, urban development and mining. “Even the bushfires from unprotected forests, negative cultural beliefs, and misconceptions that portray bats as evil make people immediately kill one [on sight],” Morenikeji says. Iya Kabirat’s daughter displaying a fruit bat pulled from a sack at the Oja-Oba market in Nigeria. (Abdullahi Jimoh for The Xylom) Last October, the Nigerian Senate passed the Endangered Species Conservation and Protection Bill, 2024, aimed at curbing wildlife trafficking and protecting wildlife. The bill, which replaces the country’s outdated 1985 wildlife legislation, awaits presidential assent. If signed into law, it would introduce fines of up to 12 million naira ($8,200) and prison terms of up to 10 years for wildlife traffickers. The bill does not specifically mention bats or provide species-specific protection for them, even when conservation groups such as Wild Africa have specifically advocated for the bill to strengthen protection for Nigerian bats. Last year, several Nigerian bat species were assessed under the IUCN Red List, including species classified as threatened. Morenikeji says bats currently lack species-specific protection under Nigerian law, although broader wildlife and environmental legislation and international rules offer some safeguards. However, Nigeria’s current Endangered Species (Control of International Trade and Traffic) (Amendment) Act, 2016 does not list bats among species prohibited from being traded or killed for consumption. But for people like Iya Kabirat who have consumed bat medicine, the risk appears to be hearsay. “People have warned that one can contract Ebola virus and other diseases from eating them,” she says, adding that she has never encountered any such instance. The growing demand is incentive enough for traders such as her to keep their business afloat. “Herbalists keep buying them,” she said. As long as they believe the concoctions work effectively, they will continue looking for them, she adds. analysis_zh.time: The report was published on 2026-09-02. The event described involves a thunderstorm in early July 2026 that caused a fig tree to fall, injuring bats. The study mentioned in the report was conducted in 2023, and the 2025 study is referenced as well.
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该事件发生在尼日利亚伊洛林,特别是在 Oja-Oba 市场。涉及的人群包括传统医药商人、草药师和当地猎人,他们以蝙蝠为食和药用目的。
analysis_zh.event: 该报告讨论了尼日利亚用蝙蝠作为传统药物的贸易,强调了人畜共患疾病 传播 的风险。它引用了 2023 年的一项研究,该研究在稻草色 果蝠 中发现了抗体,表明接触过 亨尼帕病毒 谱系 GH-M74a、尼帕病毒 和蝙蝠流感 H17N10。该报告还提到了 2025 年的一项研究,显示蝙蝠贸易参与者的卫生习惯不佳。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该报告估计,近 20% 的撒哈拉以南蝙蝠物种被猎杀是为了获取食物和药品。它指出,蝙蝠肉含有蛋白质和必需营养素,但也存在人畜共患疾病 传播 的风险。2023 年的研究发现,稻草色的 果蝠 中存在 尼帕病毒 和其他病原体的暴露,2025 年的研究则强调了贸易商和狩猎者缺乏保护措施。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 报告提到,尼日利亚参议院于2024年通过了《濒危物种保护法案》,目前正在等待总统批准。如果颁布,将对野生动物贩运实行处罚。然而,目前对蝙蝠的法律保护并不针对具体物种,报告也没有提供有关 尼帕病毒 暴发 状态或具体遏制措施的信息。

news.content: ___ Home Trends + Spotlights Politics + Issues Celebrities Hobbies + Interests Rumor Cop Search Powered by Philstar.com Interaksyon Home Trends + Spotlights Politics + Issues Celebrities Hobbies + Interests Rumor Cop Haze alert: How Filipinos can stay safe amid poor air quality By Jeline Malasig - September 2, 2026 - 7:28 PM 2585 Share Facebook Twitter A thick haze shrouds Metro Manila due to smoke from ongoing fires in Kalimantan, Indonesia, in this drone picture taken in Quezon City, Philippines, September 1, 2026.(Reuters/Adrian Portugal) The government shared tips on how Filipinos can reduce their exposure to haze following massive forest fires in Indonesia, a Southeast Asian neighbor. Parts of the Philippines have experienced poor air quality due to transboundary haze, or air pollution that has traveled hundreds of kilometers from Indonesia’s Kalimantan and Sumatra. Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency chief said the global El Niño phenomenon is a catalyst for the forest fires, although other experts have pointed to soil and land management as factors that can make certain landscapes more prone to fires. The haze consists of smoke, ash, dust and microscopic particles known as PM2.5, which are small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and potentially enter the bloodstream. The smoke and pollutants have been carried toward the Philippines by winds associated with the southwest monsoon (habagat). The Philippine Environment and Management Bureau said Filipinos may continue to be affected by the haze until September 3. Air quality may improve days afterward if widespread rainfall continues wind patterns shift. The Department of Health (DOH) warned that exposure to haze may cause difficulty breathing, coughing, chest pain, eye irritation or watery eyes. It may also worsen existing lung conditions such as asthma. It advised Filipinos to remain indoors as much as possible, keep doors and windows closed and wear an N95 face mask when going outside. It also recommended using headlights and/or fog lights when driving in low-visibility conditions. The DOH also shared tips for commuters and workers who spend much of their time on the road, including delivery riders and field workers, to protect themselves from hazy conditions. These include wearing an N95 face mask, rinsing the eyes with saline solution, drinking plenty of water and getting enough rest in a closed space away from smoke and pollution. For those without access to an N95 mask, the health agency suggested wearing a damp handkerchief or cloth to help reduce exposure to the haze. “Kung walang N95 mask at kailangang lumabas, gumamit ng basang panyo [or] damit o kaya naman ay gawin ang double-mask method bilang alternatibong paraan ng proteksyon,” the DOH said. The health agency also shared driving tips for Filipinos who may encounter hazy conditions on the road, particularly at night when visibility can be significantly reduced. These include using fog lights, observing proper speed limits, maintaining a safe distance from other vehicles, and setting the vehicle’s air-conditioning system to “recirculate” mode instead of “fresh air” mode. The DOH also explained what each air quality level means and advised people who may be affected by poor air quality to take precautions. Wear a face mask when leaving the house and avoid strenuous outdoor activities. Children, older adults, pregnant women, and people with heart or lung conditions should take extra precautions and keep their medications readily available. People working outdoors should wear a face mask and take regular breaks indoors. Motorists should drive carefully due to reduced visibility caused by the haze. The health agency said those who need help or medical assistance may call the National Emergency Hotline at 911. They may also visit health centers and YAKAP Clinics for free consultations, risk screening, laboratory tests, and medication for asthma or mild-to-moderate pneumonia. elements_zh.time: 东南亚邻国印度尼西亚发生大规模森林火灾后,政府分享了菲律宾人如何减少雾霾的建议。烟雾和污染物被西南季风(habagat)吹向菲律宾。菲律宾环境管理局表示,直到 9 月 3 日,菲律宾人可能会继续受到雾霾的影响。如果大范围降雨继续改变风型,空气质量可能会在几天后有所改善。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 由于跨境雾霾或从印度尼西亚加里曼丹和苏门答腊岛传播数百公里的空气污染,菲律宾部分地区的空气质量很差。卫生机构建议菲律宾人尽可能留在室内,关闭门窗,外出时佩戴N95口罩。它还建议在能见度较低的条件下驾驶时使用前灯和/或雾灯。儿童、老年人、孕妇以及患有心脏病或肺部疾病的人应采取额外的预防措施,并随身携带药物。
elements_zh.event: 政府向因印度尼西亚森林火灾而受到雾霾影响的菲律宾人发布了健康警告和保护措施。卫生部 (DOH) 警告说,接触雾霾可能会导致呼吸困难、咳嗽、胸痛、眼睛刺激或流泪。它还可能使现有的肺部疾病(例如哮喘)恶化。卫生部为大部分时间在路上的通勤者和工人(包括送货骑手和现场工作人员)分享了保护自己免受雾霾天气影响的建议。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 雾霾由烟雾、灰烬、灰尘和称为 PM2.5 的微小颗粒组成,这些颗粒小到足以渗透到肺部深处,并可能进入血液。卫生机构表示,需要帮助或医疗救助的人可以拨打国家紧急热线911。他们还可以前往卫生中心和YAKAP诊所进行免费咨询、风险筛查、实验室检查以及治疗哮喘或轻中度肺炎的药物。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该卫生机构解释了每个空气质量级别的含义,并建议可能受到不良空气质量影响的人们采取预防措施。它建议菲律宾人出门时戴上口罩,避免剧烈的户外活动。在户外工作的人应戴口罩并在室内定期休息。由于雾霾导致能见度降低,驾车人士应小心驾驶。

news.content: Singapore Home Australia Sydney Melbourne Brisbane Perth Gold Coast Sunshine Coast Byron Bay Hobart Adelaide Townsville New Zealand New Zealand Auckland Christchurch Queenstown Wellington Asia Bali Hong Kong Osaka Singapore Tokyo Rest of the world Barcelona Fiji London New York Paris Rome Explore U:L Home Locations Australia Sydney Melbourne Brisbane Perth Gold Coast Sunshine Coast Byron Bay Hobart Adelaide Townsville New Zealand New Zealand Auckland Christchurch Queenstown Wellington Asia Bali Hong Kong Osaka Singapore Tokyo Rest of the world Barcelona Fiji London New York Paris Rome Best Of Singapore Things To Do Food & Drink Health + Wellness Local Escapes Search U:L Search U:L Best Of Singapore Things To Do Food & Drink Health + Wellness Local Escapes News Singapore’s Haze Risk Is Rising: Everything You Need To Know 2nd Sep 2026 Written by: Gracie Stewart Singapore and Bali Editor | Urban List If Singapore suddenly starts looking a little hazy, there's a reason. The Government has been stepping up preparations for a potential haze episode, with agencies reviewing their plans as dry and hot conditions across the region increase the risk of fires—and potentially, smoke drifting our way. That doesn't mean Singapore is definitely heading for a full-blown haze crisis. Whether smoke actually reaches us depends on where fires are burning, how intense they are, wind direction and rainfall. But with conditions looking less than ideal, it's a good time to know what to look out for. So, What's Causing The Haze Risk? Much of the concern comes from fires in parts of Indonesia, particularly Sumatra and Kalimantan. Hotter and drier conditions linked to El Niño are making it easier for fires to start and spread, while the prevailing winds can potentially carry smoke towards Singapore. Singapore's Government Haze Task Force, led by the National Environment Agency, has been reviewing its preparations and has plans in place for different levels of haze. How Will You Know If The Haze Is Bad? Keep an eye on Singapore's Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) and, particularly, the one-hour PM2.5 readings. The PSI gives you a broader picture of air quality, while PM2.5 measures tiny particles that can penetrate deep into the lungs. If you're deciding whether to head out for a run, take the kids to the playground or spend the afternoon outside, the PM2.5 reading is particularly useful. As a general guide, a PSI of 101 or above is considered unhealthy. Image credit: Health Hub | Website What Does Haze Do To Your Health? Even relatively mild haze can cause irritated eyes, a scratchy throat, coughing and breathing discomfort. As the air quality worsens, the risks increase, particularly for children, older people, pregnant women and those with existing heart or lung conditions. If you develop significant breathing difficulties, chest pain or other worrying symptoms, seek medical attention. How Can You Protect Yourself? The good news is there are some very easy things you can do if the air quality deteriorates: Check the air quality: Use the myENV app or NEA's official updates rather than relying on how hazy the sky looks. Limit outdoor exercise: If the PSI rises into the unhealthy range, swap your outdoor run for an indoor workout. Keep windows and doors closed: Particularly when outdoor air quality is poor. Use an air purifier: A purifier with an appropriate filter can help reduce indoor particulate pollution. Wear an N95 if needed: If you have to spend time outdoors during unhealthy haze, a properly fitted N95 mask can help reduce exposure to fine particles. Look after kids and vulnerable family members: Consider moving outdoor play and activities indoors when air quality worsens. Should You Be Worried? Not yet, but it's worth being prepared. The Government is monitoring the situation closely, and Singapore has an established system for responding if haze levels deteriorate. So, rather than panic-buying every air purifier in Singapore, just keep an eye on the readings, dig out those N95s if you already have them and maybe have a few indoor activities ready to go.
